description: Unchanged expanded authored stages from the September 26 Codex OAuth pass, retained to reproduce the September 27 reviewed construction defects.

cases.sentence: A menina de quem falaste chegou cedo.

derivationStages.stageRecord: Merge de with the relative pronoun quem to form the PP selected by falaste. The other lexical material remains separate. The unpronounced embedded subject is represented as pro; neither finite verb is divided into separately pronounced tense and stem terminals.
derivationStages.statement: The relative-clause prepositional phrase is assembled.

derivationStages.stageRecord: Merge falaste with de quem. This complement position is the position from which the PP will later move; at this point it is still pronounced there.
derivationStages.statement: The PP occupies the embedded verb’s complement position.

derivationStages.stageRecord: Project an unpronounced v above the embedded VP and merge pro in the vP subject position. Pro is the understood second-person singular subject of falaste, not the antecedent of the relative pronoun.
derivationStages.statement: The embedded predicate receives its null subject.

derivationStages.stageRecord: Merge an abstract, unpronounced T with the embedded vP. Its past-tense and second-person singular features are expressed by the whole-word terminal falaste rather than by an additional pronounced terminal. Agreement licenses pro in its in-situ subject position.
derivationStages.statement: Finite structure licenses the embedded null subject.

derivationStages.stageRecord: Merge an unpronounced relative C with the embedded TP. The PP remains in its earlier VP-complement position until the next stage, so its movement has an independently recorded starting point.
derivationStages.statement: A relative-clause left periphery is projected.

derivationStages.stageRecord: Internally merge the entire PP de quem in the relative CP’s specifier. Its P and pronoun retain their identities and pronunciation in the higher position. The original PP occurrence remains in the VP as an unpronounced trace, accounting for the complement position of falaste. Pied-piping the P gives the surface order de quem falaste.
derivationStages.statement: The relative PP moves to the CP edge.

derivationStages.stageRecord: Project menina as an NP and adjoin the completed relative CP to it. The relative operator quem is interpreted with menina as its antecedent; the relative clause is not an argument of the main verb chegou.
derivationStages.statement: The relative clause modifies menina.

derivationStages.stageRecord: Merge the determiner A with the modified NP. The resulting DP, A menina de quem falaste, is the single subject constituent to be merged with the main predicate.
derivationStages.statement: The main-clause subject DP is assembled.

derivationStages.stageRecord: Project chegou as a VP and adjoin the AdvP cedo to that VP. This places the adverb in the main clause, where it specifies the time of arriving rather than speaking.
derivationStages.statement: Cedo modifies the arrival predicate.

derivationStages.stageRecord: Project an unpronounced main-clause v and merge the subject DP in its vP subject position. The VP containing chegou cedo remains the predicate of that DP.
derivationStages.statement: The subject enters the main predicate.

derivationStages.stageRecord: Merge an abstract T with the main vP, projecting T′ before its subject position is filled. T bears past-tense and third-person singular features expressed by the whole-word terminal chegou; it has no separately pronounced exponent here.
derivationStages.statement: The main clause receives finite T.

derivationStages.stageRecord: Internally merge the subject DP from the previously recorded vP position into the TP subject position. Its determiner and modified NP are pronounced in that higher position; the lower DP occurrence is represented as an unpronounced trace. The resulting order is A menina de quem falaste chegou cedo.
derivationStages.statement: The preverbal subject occupies the completed TP.

cases.sentence: Η Μαρία είπε ότι ο Νίκος θα φύγει αύριο.

derivationStages.stageRecord: Η Μαρία and ο Νίκος begin in their respective VP subject positions and receive their speaker and departing-entity roles there. The embedded predicate contains no temporal adjunct. The separate adjunct αύριο can instead join the matrix predicate after that predicate takes its clausal complement. The future head θα and complementizer ότι also remain separate pending construction of the embedded clause.
derivationStages.statement: Build the predicates while leaving αύριο available for matrix attachment.

derivationStages.stageRecord: The embedded verb φύγει moves to I, leaving a silent V occurrence. The embedded subject ο Νίκος then raises from VP to Spec-IP for nominative Case, leaving a silent subject occurrence. Θα projects FutP above IP, and ότι heads CP. The separate αύριο remains available for attachment to the matrix predicate.
derivationStages.statement: Complete the embedded clause without a temporal adjunct.

derivationStages.stageRecord: First the completed ότι-clause merges as the complement of είπε. The adjunct αύριο then joins a higher matrix V′, outside that complement CP. This right-adjoined position preserves the spoken order while permitting αύριο to locate the saying tomorrow rather than the departure.
derivationStages.statement: Add the CP complement and attach αύριο to the matrix predicate.

derivationStages.stageRecord: The finite matrix verb moves from V to I, leaving an unpronounced V occurrence. Neither its CP complement nor the higher matrix V′ adjunct changes position.
derivationStages.statement: Raise είπε to the matrix I head.

derivationStages.stageRecord: The matrix subject moves from VP to Spec-IP for nominative Case, leaving its lower thematic occurrence silent. The final pronounced order is unchanged from the embedded-adjunct reading, but αύριο is outside the CP and modifies the matrix saying.
derivationStages.statement: Raise Η Μαρία and complete the matrix-adjunct reading.

cases.sentence: The curator said that the painting which the students had restored was missing.

derivationStages.stageRecord: Restored heads the relative-clause VP. The students is its agent in the VP subject position, and which is its object. At this point, which has not moved.
derivationStages.statement: The relative clause begins with its subject and object in their thematic positions.

derivationStages.stageRecord: Finite had is introduced in T. The students moves from the VP subject position to Spec-TP, where it receives nominative Case. Its lower position is retained as a silent trace; which remains the object of restored.
derivationStages.statement: The relative-clause subject raises to Spec-TP.

derivationStages.stageRecord: A silent relative C projects CP above the relative TP. Which moves from the object position of restored to Spec-CP, leaving a silent object trace. The higher occurrence supplies the pronounced relative pronoun while the chain retains its object interpretation.
derivationStages.statement: Which raises to the relative-clause Spec-CP.

derivationStages.stageRecord: The relative CP adjoins to the nominal projection headed by painting, below the determiner the. Its initial which is interpreted with that nominal head, while its object trace remains inside the relative clause. The resulting DP combines with the adjectival predicate missing in a small clause, where it receives the predicate's subject role.
derivationStages.statement: The restrictive relative modifies painting, and the resulting DP is the subject of missing.

derivationStages.stageRecord: Finite copular was is introduced in T above the small clause. The painting DP moves from its predicative subject position to Spec-TP for nominative Case. The small clause retains a silent trace, and the moved DP retains the restrictive relative within its nominal projection.
derivationStages.statement: The painting which the students had restored raises to the embedded subject position.

derivationStages.stageRecord: The overt complementizer that is merged as C above the completed embedded TP. Unlike relative which, it occupies the head C position and undergoes no wh-movement.
derivationStages.statement: That introduces the finite complement clause.

derivationStages.stageRecord: The curator is merged in the matrix VP subject position, where it receives the agent role of said. Said takes the completed that-clause as its propositional complement. Matrix tense and subject raising have not yet been added.
derivationStages.statement: Said takes the that-clause as its complement.

derivationStages.stageRecord: A silent finite past T projects the matrix TP; said remains the pronounced finite verb in V. The curator moves from its VP subject position to Spec-TP for nominative Case, leaving a silent trace. The completed tree therefore distinguishes the complementizer that from the moved relative pronoun which.
derivationStages.statement: The matrix subject raises, completing the sentence.

derivationStages.stageRecord: Lena is the prospective subject of leave. The infinitival marker to and the modal must enter as distinct T heads. A silent light verb introduces the external argument; yesterday is available to modify the leaving event.
derivationStages.statement: The lexical items enter the workspace.

derivationStages.stageRecord: Merge leave into a VP and adjoin yesterday to that VP. On this attachment, yesterday locates the proposed leaving, rather than a separate time of obligation.
derivationStages.statement: Yesterday modifies the leaving event.

derivationStages.stageRecord: Merge silent v with the modified VP, then externally merge Lena in the specifier of vP. This is the position in which Lena is interpreted as the agent of leave.
derivationStages.statement: The subject receives its thematic position.

derivationStages.stageRecord: Merge infinitival to with the vP. Lena remains in its thematic position at this point; no higher subject occurrence has yet been created.
derivationStages.statement: Infinitival to heads a lower clause.

relations.relation: internal Merge to infinitival subject position

derivationStages.stageRecord: Move Lena from the vP specifier to the specifier of the infinitival TP. The lower occurrence becomes unpronounced, while the new occurrence retains Lena’s pronunciation.
derivationStages.statement: Lena occupies the infinitival subject position.

values.encountered: infinitival TP headed by overt to

derivationStages.stageRecord: Merge must with the infinitival TP. This builds the hierarchy needed for the supplied order, but it is not a licensed selection in standard English: modal must selects a bare verbal complement, not an infinitival TP headed by overt to.
derivationStages.statement: The modal is merged, exposing the selection failure.

relations.relation: internal Merge to matrix subject position

derivationStages.stageRecord: Move Lena from the infinitival subject position to the matrix subject position, leaving its intermediate occurrence unpronounced. The pronounced terminals now give exactly Lena must to leave yesterday. Raising does not repair the earlier selection failure: standard-English modal must cannot occur with this overt infinitival to as its complement.
derivationStages.statement: The surface order is complete, but the sentence is ill-formed.

cases.sentence: لم يرسل خالد الرسالة إلى أخته.

derivationStages.stageRecord: The preposition إلى merges with the DP أخته to form a PP. The possessive ending in أخته and the inflection in يرسل are treated as parts of their whole-word terminals. The verb, subject, theme, light verb, jussive T, and negative head remain separate objects.
derivationStages.statement: The recipient PP and the other lexical items are available.

derivationStages.stageRecord: The verb first merges with the theme DP. The recipient PP then adjoins to that VP, yielding the reading in which sending is directed to his sister.
derivationStages.statement: The PP is attached to the verbal predicate.

derivationStages.stageRecord: The silent light verb merges with the VP. خالد is then merged as the external argument in the specifier of vP. Its position is lower than the position the finite verb will occupy.
derivationStages.statement: The subject is merged in the verbal domain.

derivationStages.stageRecord: يرسل moves from V to the light-verbal head. Its original position is retained as an unpronounced copy; the occurrence in the higher head remains pronounced. The subject stays in the vP specifier.
derivationStages.statement: The verb raises to the light verb.

derivationStages.stageRecord: The silent jussive T merges with the existing vP. The raised verb is still in the light-verbal head at this point, so its subsequent movement to T has a distinct source position.
derivationStages.statement: Jussive T projects above vP.

derivationStages.stageRecord: The verbal complex moves from the light-verbal position to T, placing pronounced يرسل above the in-situ subject. An unpronounced copy of the complex remains in vP; the still lower V copy remains unpronounced.
derivationStages.statement: The verbal head raises to T.

derivationStages.stageRecord: The negative head لم merges with TP and licenses its jussive specification. The resulting order is لم, the verb in T, the subject in vP, the theme, and the verbal recipient PP.
derivationStages.statement: لم completes the negative clause.
